Nyirmada Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírmada, Hungary

Not demolished. The first Jew settled in Nyírmada in 1721; a synagogue was first mentioned in 1836, and by 1780 the community already had a rabbi, later adding a shochet by the mid-19th century. The organized community and its burial society formed in 1860, the same year this cemetery's land was purchased. Institutions grew steadily: a relief association, women's association, kindergarten, cheder (1870), yeshiva (1899), Talmud Torah, and an 1897 elementary school - though the original synagogue and school burned down in 1892. By 1944, the Orthodox community numbered 437 (68 taxpayers); residents were gathered at the synagogue and school on April 19 that year, then sent to the Kisvárda Ghetto four days later. Forty survivors returned after the war and briefly re-established the community, aided by the synagogue and school having survived intact, but by 1957 no Jews remained. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1838, its newest to 1944.
